statement: Prove there exist infinitely many positive integers $n$ for which $x^2 + y^{11} - z^{2022!} = n$ has no integer solution $(x,y,z)$.

In acute $\triangle ABC$ with $AB < AC$, $D, E, F$ are feet of the altitudes from $A, B, C$. Circumcircle $\Gamma$ of $\triangle AEF$ meets the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ at $A$ and $M$. Assume $BM$ is tangent to $\Gamma$. Prove $M$, $F$, $D$ are collinear.

Let $n$ be a positive integer and $x_1, \ldots, x_n \geq 0$. The \textit{transformed sequence} $y_1, \ldots, y_n$: $y_i$ is the maximum average of a consecutive sub-sequence containing $x_i$. Prove: (a) For any $t > 0$, $|\{i : y_i > t\}| \leq \frac{2}{t}(x_1+\cdots+x_n)$. (b) $\dfrac{y_1+\cdots+y_n}{32n} \leq \sqrt{\dfrac{x_1^2+\cdots+x_n^2}{32n}}$.
In $\triangle ABC$ with incenter $I$, the incircle touches $BC$ at $D$. $P$ on ray $IB$ and $Q$ on ray $IC$ satisfy $\angle IAP = \angle CAD$ and $\angle IAQ = \angle BAD$. Prove $AP = AQ$.

$n \geq 4$ lines in general position (no two parallel, no three concurrent) have $\binom{n}{2}$ intersection points each with $k$ coins. Ana and Beto alternately remove a coin from a point not on any common line with the previous point. First unable to move loses; Ana starts. Determine who wins based on $n$ and $k$.

A positive integer $N$ is on a board. Each round Olive may: (1) replace $N$ by any positive multiple; (2) replace $N$ by any rearrangement of its digits (leading zeros allowed). Find all $N$ for which Olive can reach 1.
